body.statement: Whenever Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser return an identifying functional using only selector values in \(H\) and denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})\), \(\operatorname{SA\mbox{-}CS\mbox{-}ID}\) returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\) such that \(O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H\) and \(F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\). Gate reinsertion makes the returned circuit and its required positive margins algebraically equal to the published derivation on the original expansion.
body.justification: This is now supported by an input-determined simulation theorem rather than by installing the successful published derivation as the machine agenda.
body.gap: The new proof closes preservation for support-licensed successful branches while keeping residual completeness logically separate.
body.consumer: Existing systematic-selection formulas can be replayed on the normalized backend with the same supported margins and no added selector context.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a successful published derivation satisfying the two hypotheses. By \(\textnormal{lem:published-trace-scheduling}\), the input-determined machine simulates its recursive tasks in dependency-topological order. In particular, after every scheduled step its labelled normalized kernels equal the corresponding published kernels after gate reinsertion, its remaining worklist is the unexecuted suffix, and it has registered exactly the same context masses and fixing margins. The simulation lemma also shows that this successful path cannot be sent to a residual failure state.

For completeness, the initial equality used by the simulation is
\[
 q_s(v)=\frac{p_H(v,s)}{p_H(S=s)},
 \qquad
 p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v,s)>0,
\tag{7}
\]
for every published context \(s\in H\). At a prescribed fixing step the two constructions use the same margin
\[
 m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D},
\tag{8}
\]
and the equality of predecessor and successor descriptions is the exact cross-multiplied identity \(m_{s,W}(K_{s,D}/m_{s,W})=K_{s,D}\). At an ancestor marginalization or a district split, finite distributivity gives the same ordered sum--product circuit. These are the algebraic equalities, not additional identifying assumptions.

Let \(F_H=P/D\) be the accumulated reduced terminal circuit. The proof of \(\textnormal{lem:published-trace-scheduling}\) gives
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=0\pmod{\mathcal J},
\tag{9}
\]
and therefore the residual verifier accepts the compiled projection candidate. Every factor of \(D\) is one of the supported context normalizers, one of the margins in (8), or a reduced factor with the exact ledger decomposition produced by the task invariant. The frozen result \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\) consequently gives
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{10}
\]

The terminal published circuit is identifying by the premise of the theorem. Equation (9), the stepwise circuit equality, and \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) give, for every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\),
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}
 =F_H\bigl(O_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}\bigr)
 =T_{a,H}^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}
 =T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{11}
\]
All divisions in (11) are licensed by (10). Every context used in (7)--(11) belongs to \(H\), so the construction neither conditions on nor supplies a law from an absent context. This proves the claim.
